stem: The processes that maintain and sustain life, such as nutrition and respiration, are called __________.
solution: Life processes are the basic functions (nutrition, respiration, transportation, excretion, etc.) that keep an organism alive.

stem: The process by which organisms obtain and utilise food is called __________.
solution: Nutrition is the process of taking in and using food for energy, growth and repair.

stem: Green plants make their own food and are therefore called __________.
solution: Autotrophs like green plants make their own food by photosynthesis.

stem: The raw materials for photosynthesis are carbon dioxide, water, sunlight and __________.
solution: Photosynthesis requires carbon dioxide, water, sunlight and chlorophyll to produce glucose and oxygen.

stem: The tiny pores on leaves through which gaseous exchange occurs are the __________.
solution: Stomata are pores in the leaf epidermis for gas exchange and transpiration.

stem: Amoeba obtains its food by engulfing it using __________.
solution: Amoeba engulfs food using pseudopodia (false feet), forming a food vacuole.

stem: The acid secreted in the human stomach that helps digestion and kills germs is __________.
solution: The stomach secretes hydrochloric acid, which aids digestion and kills microbes.

stem: The enzyme in saliva that begins the digestion of starch is __________.
solution: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) begins the breakdown of starch in the mouth.

stem: Most of the digestion and absorption of food occurs in the __________.
solution: The small intestine completes digestion and absorbs most of the digested food.

stem: The finger-like projections that increase the absorptive surface of the small intestine are the __________.
solution: Villi increase the surface area of the small intestine for efficient absorption.

stem: The bile juice, which helps digest fats, is secreted by the __________.
solution: Bile, secreted by the liver, emulsifies fats to aid their digestion.

stem: The release of energy from food inside the cell is called __________.
solution: Cellular respiration breaks down glucose to release energy for the cell.

stem: Aerobic respiration takes place in the presence of oxygen and produces __________.
options: carbon dioxide, water and a large amount of energy
solution: Aerobic respiration produces carbon dioxide, water and more energy than anaerobic respiration.

stem: In our muscles during vigorous exercise, glucose is broken down without oxygen to form __________.
solution: Anaerobic respiration in muscles produces lactic acid, causing cramps.

stem: The organelle where most energy is released during respiration is the __________.
solution: Mitochondria, the powerhouses of the cell, are where most cellular respiration (energy release) occurs.

stem: The energy released during respiration is stored in the molecule __________.
solution: Energy released in respiration is stored as ATP (adenosine triphosphate), the energy currency of the cell.

stem: The tiny air sacs in the lungs where gas exchange occurs are the __________.
solution: Alveoli are the tiny air sacs in the lungs where oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged with the blood.

stem: The respiratory pigment in human blood that carries oxygen is __________.
solution: Haemoglobin in red blood cells binds and carries oxygen throughout the body.

stem: The transport system in humans that carries blood is the __________ system.
solution: The circulatory system transports blood, carrying oxygen, nutrients and wastes.

stem: The muscular organ that pumps blood throughout the body is the __________.
solution: The heart pumps blood around the body.

stem: The human heart has __________ chambers.
solution: The human heart has four chambers — two atria and two ventricles.

stem: The upper chambers of the heart are the __________.
solution: The two upper chambers of the heart are the atria, which receive blood.

stem: The blood vessels that carry blood away from the heart are the __________.
solution: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, usually oxygen-rich blood.

stem: The blood vessels that carry blood back to the heart are the __________.
solution: Veins carry blood back to the heart.

stem: The double circulation in humans means blood passes through the heart __________ in one complete cycle.
solution: In double circulation, blood passes through the heart twice per cycle (pulmonary and systemic circuits).

stem: Water and minerals are transported in plants through the __________.
solution: Xylem transports water and minerals from the roots to the rest of the plant.

stem: Food prepared in the leaves is transported to other parts of the plant through the __________.
solution: Phloem transports food (sugars) from the leaves to other plant parts (translocation).

stem: The loss of water as vapour from the aerial parts of a plant is called __________.
solution: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from a plant, mainly through the stomata.

stem: Transpiration helps in the upward movement of water in plants by creating a __________.
solution: Transpiration creates a suction (transpiration pull) that draws water up the xylem.

stem: The removal of harmful metabolic wastes from the body is called __________.
solution: Excretion is the removal of metabolic waste products from the body.

stem: The main excretory organs in humans are the __________.
solution: The kidneys filter the blood and remove wastes as urine.

stem: The basic filtration unit of the kidney is the __________.
solution: The nephron is the functional (filtration) unit of the kidney.

stem: The main nitrogenous waste excreted by humans in urine is __________.
solution: Urea is the chief nitrogenous waste excreted by the kidneys in urine.

stem: When the kidneys fail, wastes are removed from the blood by a process called __________.
solution: Dialysis artificially filters the blood to remove wastes when the kidneys fail.

stem: Plants excrete some waste products by storing them in leaves that fall off, or as __________.
solution: Plants store or release wastes as gums, resins, and in leaves/bark that are shed; some gases are released via stomata.

stem: The largest gland in the human body, which has many functions including bile secretion, is the __________.
solution: The liver is the largest gland; it secretes bile and performs many metabolic functions.

stem: The pancreas secretes the enzyme that digests fats, called __________.
solution: Pancreatic lipase digests fats; the pancreas also secretes enzymes for proteins and carbohydrates.

stem: The exchange of gases in plants and animals occurs by the process of __________.
solution: Gases move in and out of cells and organs mainly by diffusion, down their concentration gradients.

stem: Fish breathe using __________ to extract oxygen dissolved in water.
solution: Fish use gills to obtain oxygen dissolved in water.

stem: The valves in the heart and veins ensure that blood flows in __________.
solution: Valves prevent the backflow of blood, ensuring it flows in one direction.

stem: The blood pressure is measured using an instrument called a __________.
solution: A sphygmomanometer measures blood pressure.

stem: The lymphatic system helps in transport by carrying __________.
options: lymph (a fluid that drains from tissues)
solution: The lymphatic system carries lymph, absorbs fats from the intestine, and drains extra fluid from tissues.

stem: In plants, water absorbed by roots enters the root hairs mainly by __________.
solution: Water enters root hair cells by osmosis, moving from the soil into the cells.

stem: Which of the following correctly matches a life process with its function?
solution: Respiration releases energy from food. (Excretion removes wastes, nutrition provides food, transportation carries materials.)

stem: The chlorophyll needed for photosynthesis is present in the organelle called the __________.
solution: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.

stem: During the day, plants release __________ as a by-product of photosynthesis.
solution: Photosynthesis releases oxygen as a by-product during the day.

stem: Which of the following is TRUE about the human circulatory system?
options: It carries oxygen and nutrients to cells and removes wastes
solution: The circulatory system transports oxygen and nutrients to cells and carries away carbon dioxide and wastes.

stem: Herbivores have a longer small intestine than carnivores because __________.
options: plant food (cellulose) takes longer to digest
solution: Cellulose-rich plant food is harder to digest, so herbivores have a longer intestine.

stem: The correct sequence of steps in nutrition in humans is __________.
solution: Nutrition proceeds as ingestion, digestion, absorption, assimilation and egestion.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Life Processes' is that:
options: living organisms carry out nutrition, respiration, transportation and excretion through specialised systems to sustain life
living things need no processes to survive
solution: The chapter explains the essential life processes — nutrition, respiration, transportation and excretion — in plants and animals.
